name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: Ballots drop today!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
Together, we can move the Democratic Party in a more progressive direction.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260717-6488-footer&t=1&akid=6488%2E420207%2Edcfu_K)
Peter,
Voting in the Washington state primary starts today, with ballots on the way to voters as we speak.
We’ve spent the last year and a half building something extraordinary. Training over 30,000 people in nonviolent resistance. Rallying, marching, standing up to illegal wars, fighting to protect immigrant communities, and refusing to back down from the Trump administration’s march toward authoritarianism.
**Now is the time to turn our resistance into votes and show the strength of our progressive movement.**
For everyone in Seattle and King County, I want to encourage you to cast your vote in the primary for these bold, progressive candidates who I am proud to endorse:
* **Liz Berry** for the 36th Legislative District, House
* **Jaelynn Scott** for the 37th Legislative District, House
* **Gerry Pollet** for the 46th Legislative District, House
* **Darya Farivar** for the 46th Legislative District, House
* **Colleen Melody** for the Washington Supreme Court, Position 1
* **Jaime Hawk** for the Washington Supreme Court, Position 3
* **Ian Birk** for the Washington Supreme Court, Position 4
* **Jorge Barón** for King County Council, District 4
* **Teresa Mosqueda** for King County Council, District 8

I also want to invite everyone — whether you’re here in Washington or outside the state — to volunteer with our team as we work to get proud progressives across the finish line.
[**You can click here to find both in-person and virtual volunteer opportunities between now and Election Day.**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/42755?org_ids=3581%3Futm_source%3Dem20260717-6488&t=2&akid=6488%2E420207%2Edcfu_K)
**[Volunteer Now](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/42755?org_ids=3581%3Futm_source%3Dem20260717-6488&t=3&akid=6488%2E420207%2Edcfu_K)**
Together, we can organize, win, and build a more progressive Democratic Party – taking back the House and electing local leaders who will put working families first.
In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

name: Squad Victory Fund
subject: What real representation looks like
body:

Peter,

We have less than a month left until Ilhan's primary election on August
11th, and she’s up against a former ICE prosecutor — the very agency that
terrorized our communities and brought destruction, even death, to
innocent civilians across Minnesota and our country.

We cannot let Ilhan's challenger take her seat.

Ilhan is one of the toughest fighters in Congress, and she doesn’t back
down, not from Trump, not from his MAGA machine, not from the billionaires
who would love nothing more than to silence her.

She is fighting for economic justice for working families, for affordable
healthcare and reproductive rights, for housing for all, and for racial
justice. And Ilhan delivers.

During her time in Congress, Ilhan has protected the Liberian-American
community from deportation, brought home over $550,000 in casework for her
constituents, and helped lead the fight for the Inflation Reduction Act,
the largest climate action plan in world history. She's also secured over
$65 million for community projects across Minnesota's Fifth District, and
been a leading voice for a just, humane foreign policy.

This is what real representation looks like, and it's exactly why we have
to have her back right now ahead of her primary.

That's what the Squad Victory Fund exists to do. We run on people power,
not corporate PAC money or special interests, and that means we only win
when this grassroots team shows up for leaders like Ilhan. With August
11th closing in fast, this is the moment she needs us most.

| | Peter, **Today, I am suspending my campaign for Alaska's at-large House seat.** I entered this race because I believe public service is a moral calling, and because too many Alaskans feel unheard in the fight for a fairer, more just world. I am deeply disappointed that the GOP chose to meddle in this race, and that too many institutions within the Democratic Party ecosystem declined to meaningfully support a campaign rooted in service, integrity, and the needs of working Alaskans. But we are living through a moment when our democracy itself is under threat, and defeating Nick Begich and restoring a Democratic majority in the House must come before any one candidate or campaign. It has become clear to me in recent days that remaining in this race no longer serves that urgent purpose. That's why I'm suspending my campaign and calling on Democrats, Independents, and all Alaskans who believe in protecting our democracy to vote for Bill Hill in the general election this November. **I want to close out by saying thank you.** To everyone who knocked on doors, made calls, hosted a gathering in your living room, or talked to a neighbor about why this election matters: **thank you.** To everyone who gave five dollars or five hundred, who signed up to volunteer even when your schedule was already full, who put a sign in your yard or shared a post because you believed in what we were building:**thank you.** None of this happened because of me. It happened because Alaskans showed up for each other, and that is the truest measure of what our campaign was about. **Suspending our campaign does not mean stepping away from the fight.** My faith teaches me that we are called to seek justice, care for our neighbors, and stand against systems that put wealth and power ahead of people, and I will continue answering that call, within this election cycle and beyond. I will keep fighting for a more just world, for a government that serves people first, and to get big money and the influence of out-of-state billionaires out of our politics. I am deeply grateful to every Alaskan who placed their trust in our campaign, and I look forward to continuing this work alongside you. I'll have more to share in the weeks ahead about celebrations to thank supporters like you, Peter. We're not going anywhere. Thank you for everything, _Rev. Matt Schultz_ __ |
---|---|---

To everyone who gave five dollars or five hundred, who signed up to volunteer even when your schedule was already full, who put a sign in your yard or shared a post because you believed in what we were building:thank you. None of this happened because of me. It happened because Alaskans showed up for each other, and that is the truest measure of what our campaign was about. Suspending our campaign does not mean stepping away from the fight. My faith teaches me that we are called to seek justice, care for our neighbors, and stand against systems that put wealth and power ahead of people, and I will continue answering that call, within this election cycle and beyond. I will keep fighting for a more just world, for a government that serves people first, and to get big money and the influence of out-of-state billionaires out of our politics. I am deeply grateful to every Alaskan who placed their trust in our campaign, and I look forward to continuing this work alongside you. I'll have more to share in the weeks ahead about celebrations to thank supporters like you, Peter. We're not going anywhere. Thank you for everything, Rev. Matt Schultz | ---|---|--- | | | Paid for and authorized by Matt Schultz for Alaska. |

| | | | | | Friend,
Today, former Las Cruces Mayor Ken Miyagishima announced that he is ending his campaign for Governor and joining ours.
In announcing his endorsement, Ken shared:
_**“I realized that the best way to make a difference in New Mexico is by teaming up with my good friend, and former Mayor Gregg Hull.”**_
Ken and I did not enter this race from the same political party. We served different cities in different parts of our state. Yet as mayors, we faced many of the same challenges, and we learned that potholes are not Republican or Democratic, public safety is not a partisan issue, and creating good jobs should never take a back seat to political games.
We both know what it means to lead a city, balance a budget, work with people from every background, and be held accountable for real results.
That is why Ken’s endorsement matters.
This campaign is becoming a place where New Mexicans can come together around something bigger than party labels: safer communities, a stronger economy, better schools, responsible leadership, and a state government that works for the people it serves.
Ken could have stepped away from this race quietly. Instead, he chose to stand with us and help build the coalition needed to win in November.
**Now I am asking you to stand with us too.**
Our opponent will have millions of dollars and a national fundraising network behind her. We are building something different: a New Mexico campaign powered by people ready to move our state in a new direction.
**Will you contribute $25, $50, $100, or another amount today to help us share this endorsement across New Mexico and reach the voters who will decide this election?**

# **Get Access to In-person, Storm Recovery Resources This Weekend**
# _Saturday to Monday_
_[](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172097.173029.726&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17978)_ From Saturday to Monday, [Philadelphia's Office of Emergency Management](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172097.173029.726&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17978) will be hosting pop-up resource fairs to connect in-person with Philadelphia residents that need help with storm recovery. [](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172097.173029.726&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17978) The following agencies and departments will be available to answer questions and provide support: **[Learn more at the City of Philadelphia website! ](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172097.173029.726&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17978)******
* * *
**Hear From Senator Hughes and City and State Leaders About Storm Recovery** **** Join us for a telephone townhall on **Saturday, July 18th, from 12PM to 1PM** to hear from Senator Hughes, **the Philadelphia Office of Emergency Management, the PA Emergency Management Agency, the PA Department of Insurance, and PECO**. Participants will be able to ask live questions and learn about important resources that can help with storm recovery.
* * *
**Stay in Touch on Social Media** If you haven't visited Senator Hughes' [**Facebook page**](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172097.173029.726&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17979), join the conversation by 'liking' the page and following our office on [**Instagram**](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172097.173029.726&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17980), [**TikTok**](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172097.173029.726&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17981), [**X**](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172097.173029.726&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17982), and [**Bluesky**](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172097.173029.726&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17971),. We have lots of information available on these pages about community events and issues affecting our district. If you have questions or concerns, send us an email at [**hughes@pasenate.com**](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172097.173029.726&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17972).

subject: Election System Vulnerabilities Exposed
body:
Justice Dept Joins California Voter Roll Lawsuit

[INSIDE JW]

THE INTELLIGENCE COMMUNITY WITHHELD ELECTION-SYSTEM VULNERABILITIES

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84191&L=38242&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g/dj1PR3kwZmh4aFlNTSZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=f9d24ad90618785b5257fbdb9e683e8a35f6e012aee784909efa04e203a2dbcc]

In March 2025, President Trump issued an executive order
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84191&L=34850&F=T&&hash=eaa6e88f75969f6e04393534ab5a0261c86474fdfb1b76736f49ab3a0de49dea]
that included a directive to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security
to review the security of electronic voting systems.

In an April 2025 White House Cabinet meeting, then-Director of
National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard indicated
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84191&L=36259&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly90aGVuZXdhbWVyaWNhbi5jb20vdXMvcG9saXRpY3MvZG5pLWdhYmJhcmQtY29uZmlybXMtZWxlY3Rpb24tbWFjaGluZXMtY2hhbmdlLXZvdGVzLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=0d265d96d4439ee1ae8955e74010bd82d82887d6bd7c956f8d942ebec24d0f80]
that voting machines are susceptible to hacking and capable of
changing votes. “We have evidence of how these electronic voting
systems have been vulnerable to hackers for a very long time, and
vulnerable to exploitation to manipulate the results of the votes
being cast.”

We’re on the case.

We forced the release of 8 pages
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84191&L=38232&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL29kbmktZWxlY3Ryb25pYy12b3RpbmctbWFjaGluZS1yZWNvcmRzLTAzNTI2Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=71c10a6b8c48db0193b356e272e61c683d8010b9438eb2ae4e472ef151f2dcbb]
of documents from the Office of the Director of National Intelligence
(ODNI) in a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit that show that
an ODNI task force stated that the Intelligence Community identified
election-system vulnerabilities that could be exploited by U.S.
adversaries and withheld information about those vulnerabilities from
the American people.

We filed the lawsuit
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84191&L=36284&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvdHVsc2ktZ2FiYmFyZC1jYWJpbmV0LW1lZXRpbmcvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=0989151b9b51ae9a7472fa6ffd5849a51374107ab39aba051343c0cd318791e3] after
ODNI failed to respond to an April 2025 request concerning
vulnerabilities in electronic voting systems (_J_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84191&L=38243&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtb2RuaS1nYWJiYXJkLWNvbXBsYWludC0wMzUyNi9dX3VkaWNpYWw/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=d25c5e49715ab89f5e26c387215868cb4a9f302afd6b20ce5fbcd6feac8192ec
Watch Inc. v. Office of the Director of National Intelligence_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84191&L=36258&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtb2RuaS1nYWJiYXJkLWNvbXBsYWludC0wMzUyNi8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=bad6ad4a0dc59ac1503dd7e8218cdcdd5d3c12c898495de6c6da385da0478b35]
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84191&L=38233&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtb2RuaS1nYWJiYXJkLWNvbXBsYWludC0wMzUyNi9dKE5vP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=b5ec3feef2c44b0edb896dc5e04203d6649d44f755537839676e570c619b7e41.
1:25-cv-03526)).

In an April 9, 2025, message
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84191&L=38234&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtb2RuaS1lbGVjdHJvbmljLXZvdGluZy1tYWNoaW5lLXJlY29yZHMtMDM1MjYtcGdzLTctMTAvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=aad64da8a707e730bbf0cc8c59846ddecfeca3c65ae0f91921102f2bf822f942]
containing proposed talking points, the press secretary for the Office
of the Director of National Intelligence writes:

> The DIG [Director’s Initiatives Group] has uncovered indications
> of bias and politicization within the intelligence community’s
> election security assessments. Specifically, the DIG has uncovered
> indications that intelligence community [redacted] had identified
> election system vulnerabilities that could be exploited by our
> adversaries and proceeded to withhold or [redacted] this information
> from the American people.

> (The Director in the meeting yesterday asked for the ugly truth
> hard-hitting information)

> The DIG is working overtime interviewing whistleblowers and
> reviewing documents necessary to declassify election related IC
> products.

An April 10, 2025, email chain
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84191&L=38235&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtb2RuaS1lbGVjdHJvbmljLXZvdGluZy1tYWNoaW5lLXJlY29yZHMtMDM1MjYtcGdzLTMtNi8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=f2fc47b357d72cefe58964a098d4e5aaec44370b8ebb119498eaf37d0f3da375],
from a person whose name is redacted to the deputy chief of staff for
ODNI states:

> 1. The DIG is conducting a broad review of all election related IC
> products, assessments, and reports for political bias and
> suppression of critical intelligence.
>
> 2. The DIG is conducting a fresh assessment of voting systems
> security leveraging cutting edge technology and cyber experts.
>
> 3. The DIG is supporting on-going DOJ investigations with a nexus to
> election security and interference.
>
> ***
>
> The DIG is pursuing an inquiry into open-source information from the
> State Commission of Elections for Puerto Rico that Dominion voting
> machines produced hundreds of vote total discrepancies, machines
> reversed totals, under counted votes, and/or reported zero votes for
> some candidates. This appears to be the best real-world example of
> Dominion voting machines doing exactly what the company claimed was
> impossible to do from a reputable state entity.
>
> ***
>
> The DIG met with US Attorney Muldrow and his team today ... to
> coordinate DIG support to on-going DOJ investigations looking
> specifically into foreign influence, election interference,
> counterintelligence, corruption, money laundering, and drug
> trafficking.
>
> The DIG inquiries ... will continue to conduct a proper hand-off
> and/or criminal referral to DOJ via our FBI detailee.
>
> ***
>
> It does not appear Dominion has a good excuse for what happened and
> we want to get our hands on the machines before potential evidence
> is erased. I feel this may be our best opportunity to document how
> election rigging “is” occurring and then use that signature to
> walk back through IC records to search for the same fingerprints.

We urge the Trump administration to release all documents under law
about its findings on electronic voting machine vulnerabilities. Our
democracy may be at stake.

We are a national leader in voting integrity and voting rights. As
part of our work, we assembled a team of highly experienced election
law attorneys who stopped discriminatory elections in Hawaii, and
cleaned up voter rolls in California, Ohio, Indiana, and Kentucky,
among other achievements
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84191&L=38236&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvdGFnL2VsZWN0aW9uLWxhdz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=24e47a41a262aa3f528f8b247e5fd46cc310b0014c48f47b5d9b952cdbabf3ec].

The U.S. Department of Justice recently filed a motion to intervene
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84191&L=38222&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvdW5pdGVkLXN0YXRlcy1zZWVrcy10by1pbnRlcnZlbmUtaW4tanVkaWNpYWwtd2F0Y2gtbGF3c3VpdC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=355381973ae7b88b51dc3111d6dd5185cbb47281bf9b2b89676a4b52aab03cae]
in our federal lawsuit filed on behalf of a California political
candidate and a state political party against the State of California
due to its failure to maintain accurate voter rolls as required by the
National Voter Registration Act (NVRA).

In May 2026, we filed a federal lawsuit
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84191&L=37913&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvY2FsaWZvcm5pYS1jbGVhbi11cC1pbmFjdGl2ZS12b3Rlci1yZWdpc3RyYXRpb25zLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=7a055b1ada63e936714657931ff785b64719547d30a49ee7265cbceeb15d40ae]
on behalf of a California political candidate and a state political
party against the State of California due to its failure to maintain
accurate voter rolls as required by the National Voter Registration
Act (NVRA).

Our lawsuits and legal actions have caused the removal
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84191&L=37547&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvaW5hY3RpdmUtdm90ZXJzLXJlbW92ZWQtY29sb3JhZG8tdm90ZXItcm9sbHMvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=7998d82757f5f93bb7c9c88992f1149d2e0d24d3f69c9713f37490381c48f097]
of six million ineligible names from voter lists nationwide.

Earlier this year, we earned a victory
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84191&L=36862&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvc3RhdGVtZW50LW9uLXN1cHJlbWUtY291cnQtdmljdG9yeS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=2271473f8fb68a8a2fed09f900070a0aa570c1f3e62fddfd04df8bc974657e7a] at
the Supreme Court upholding the right of candidates to challenge
ballot counting rules that allowed the counting of late-arriving
ballots. In a 7-2 decision, the court held that Congressman Mike Bost
and two presidential electors had standing to challenge an Illinois
law allowing ballots received up to 14 days after Election Day to be
counted.

U.S. to Intervene in Lawsuit to Force California to Clean Up Voter
Rolls

Here’s confirmation that we’re on the right track in California.

The U.S. Department of Justice has filed a motion to intervene
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84191&L=38219&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL3dhZ25lci12LXdlYmVyLWNhLW52cmEtbW90aW9uLXRvLWludGVydmVuZS0wMTI2My8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=1b76f290d4bd9b8247e1555b1eb3c22f832105c26c32a1a1cf14d2759d51811e]
in our federal lawsuit filed on behalf of a California political
candidate and a state political party against the State of California
due to its failure to maintain accurate voter rolls as required by the
National Voter Registration Act (NVRA).

The United States filed its motion and a proposed complaint in
intervention in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of
California in our May 2026 lawsuit
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84191&L=37913&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvY2FsaWZvcm5pYS1jbGVhbi11cC1pbmFjdGl2ZS12b3Rlci1yZWdpc3RyYXRpb25zLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=7a055b1ada63e936714657931ff785b64719547d30a49ee7265cbceeb15d40ae]
(_Don Wagner et al. v. Shirley N. Weber, in her official capacity as
California Secretary of State_

The Justice Department is right to follow our lead. It is on target in
calling California’s voting rolls ‘among the worst in the
nation.’ Our lawsuits and legal action have already caused the
removal of six million dirty voter names from the rolls. Another
million or so must be cleaned.

The Justice Department’s proposed complaint in intervention names
California Secretary of State Shirley Weber as a defendant and states
the intervention was filed “to enforce provisions of the National
Voter Registration and the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (HAVA).”

Federal law requires most inactive voter registrations to be removed
after two general federal elections. Our lawsuit alleges, based on
admissions in prior Judicial Watch litigation, that 873,092 California
voter registrations have remained continuously inactive for at least
three federal elections, and some for much longer. Of these
registrations, 326,808 have remained continuously inactive through at
least three consecutive federal general elections, while 151,202 have
remained inactive through at least four consecutive federal general
elections.

In addition, 33,922 voter registrations have remained continuously
inactive through at least five consecutive federal general elections
— dating back at least ten years, to before the November 5, 2016,
presidential election.

The DIG inquiries ... will continue to conduct a proper hand-off and/or criminal referral to DOJ via our FBI detailee. * It does not appear Dominion has a good excuse for what happened and we want to get our hands on the machines before potential evidence is erased. I feel this may be our best opportunity to document how election rigging “is” occurring and then use that signature to walk back through IC records to search for the same fingerprints. The U.S. Department of Justice recently filed a motion to intervene [] in our federal lawsuit filed on behalf of a California political candidate and a state political party against the State of California due to its failure to maintain accurate voter rolls as required by the National Voter Registration Act (NVRA). Our lawsuits and legal actions have caused the removal [] of six million ineligible names from voter lists nationwide. U.S. to Intervene in Lawsuit to Force California to Clean Up Voter Rolls Here’s confirmation that we’re on the right track in California. The U.S. Department of Justice has filed a motion to intervene [] in our federal lawsuit filed on behalf of a California political candidate and a state political party against the State of California due to its failure to maintain accurate voter rolls as required by the National Voter Registration Act (NVRA). The United States filed its motion and a proposed complaint in intervention in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California in our May 2026 lawsuit [] (Don Wagner et al. v. Shirley N. Weber, in her official capacity as California Secretary of State [ (No. 8:26-cv-01263)). The Justice Department is right to follow our lead. It is on target in calling California’s voting rolls ‘among the worst in the nation.’ Our lawsuits and legal action have already caused the removal of six million dirty voter names from the rolls. Another million or so must be cleaned. The Justice Department’s proposed complaint in intervention names California Secretary of State Shirley Weber as a defendant and states the intervention was filed “to enforce provisions of the National Voter Registration and the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (HAVA).” Federal law requires most inactive voter registrations to be removed after two general federal elections. Our lawsuit alleges, based on admissions in prior Judicial Watch litigation, that 873,092 California voter registrations have remained continuously inactive for at least three federal elections, and some for much longer. Of these registrations, 326,808 have remained continuously inactive through at least three consecutive federal general elections, while 151,202 have remained inactive through at least four consecutive federal general elections. In addition, 33,922 voter registrations have remained continuously inactive through at least five consecutive federal general elections — dating back at least ten years, to before the November 5, 2016, presidential election. Under the National Voter Registration Act of 1993 (NVRA []), states are required to make reasonable efforts to remove ineligible voters from the voter rolls, including those who have died or moved. The lawsuit also alleges, again citing admissions by California officials, that the state takes no effective action to require counties to comply with the NVRA. As a result, they do not comply. The lawsuit was filed on behalf of Don Wagner, an elected member of the Orange County Board of Supervisors and candidate for California Secretary of State, and the American Independent Party of California. We are assisted by the Benbrook Law Group of Sacramento, California. We are a national leader in election integrity and voting rights litigation, with a record of successful lawsuits [] enforcing constitutional redistricting standards and cleaning voter rolls nationwide. Our lawsuits and legal actions have caused the removal [] of six million ineligible names from voter lists nationwide. Robert Popper, a Judicial Watch senior attorney, leads our election law program. Popper was previously in the Voting Section of the Civil Rights Division of the Justice Department, where he managed voting rights investigations, litigations, consent decrees, and settlements in dozens of states. In April 2026, we announced a settlement [] in our federal lawsuit against Oregon election officials, which confirms 800,000 [] ineligible voter names are slated for review and removal from voter registration lists. Colorado recently removed 372,000 ineligible voter names thanks to a Judicial Watch lawsuit and settlement [] addressing the state’s compliance with federal voter list maintenance requirements. In Kentucky, state election board officials reported [] that “roughly 735,000 ineligible voter registrations” have been removed from voter rolls, as part of a 2018 consent decree settling a Judicial Watch lawsuit. As part of its 2022 settlement [], New York City alone has removed 918,139 ineligible names from its rolls: data show 477,056 [] removals between March 2023 and February 2025, which is in addition to the 441,083 previously reported removals. Our legal pressure also resulted in election roll clean-ups in Pennsylvania [], North Carolina [], and Ohio []. A federal court in Illinois [] has ruled that our lawsuit to force the cleaning of voter rolls may proceed in that state. In January 2026, in a historic case we filed, the Supreme Court decided 7-2 [] in favor of Congressman Mike Bost and two presidential electors who were before the court to vindicate their standing to challenge an Illinois law allowing the counting of ballots received up to 14 days after Election Day. JUDICIAL WATCH SUES FOR FBI MEMORANDUM ON FISA TARGETING We’re wading deeper into the Deep State swamp. We filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit [] against the U.S. Department of Justice for an interagency memorandum of understanding between the FBI and an agency the name of which is redacted regarding the targeting and minimization procedures referenced in a Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court opinion (Judicial Watch Inc. v. U.S. Department of Justice [ (No. 1:26-cv-02407)). We sued after the FBI failed to respond to a March 10, 2026, FOIA request for a copy of the memorandum that is cited in a footnote on page 87 of an opinion [] by Judge Rosemary Collyer filed on April 26, 2017. The footnote we reference states: The improper access granted to the [redacted] contractors was apparently in place [redacted] and seems to have been the result of deliberate decisionmaking. [Redacted] Compliance Report at 92-93 ([redacted] access to FBI systems was the subject of an interagency memorandum of understanding entered into [redacted]). Despite the existence of an interagency memorandum of understanding (presumably prepared or reviewed by FBI lawyers), no notice of this practice was given to the FISC until 2016. Of course, such a memorandum of understanding could not override the restrictions of Section 702 minimization procedures. The Office of the Director of National Intelligence explains that Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) Section 702 [] is a U.S. intelligence provision that “only permits the targeting of non-United States persons who are reasonably believed to be located outside the United States. United States persons and anyone in the United States may not be targeted.” Further, “all Section 702 targets must be non-United States persons reasonably believed to be located outside the United States ... such targets may send an email or have a phone call with a United States person. For this reason, Section 702 requires specific procedures to minimize the acquisition, retention, and sharing of any information concerning United States persons.” The Obama FBI had officially opened its investigation, code-named “Crossfire Hurricane,” into the campaign of then-presidential candidate Donald Trump on July 31, 2016. The court’s 99-page opinion [] documents significant compliance failures involving FISA surveillance during the same period [], raising concerns about the handling of raw intelligence information and compliance with court-ordered minimization procedures. This undisclosed FBI agreement was in effect during one of the most controversial periods in U.S. history, when Crossfire Hurricane and other FISA-related activities were under way. The American people should not have to wait one more day for transparency. We have led efforts to uncover much of what the public knows about Crossfire Hurricane/Russiagate, which involved a long list of Democratic political figures, lawyers, and staffers who shaped the narrative around the Trump-Russia hoax. In January 2026, we sued [] the Justice Department for fully unredacted records and previously withheld or missing portions of former Special Counsel John Durham’s investigation into the origins of the Crossfire Hurricane/Russiagate investigation. In October 2020, we uncovered [] heavily redacted email communications among top-level State Department officials and a U.S. ambassador expressing skepticism about reports by Christopher Steele’s London-based private intelligence firm Orbis Business Intelligence. (Steele was the author of the Clinton-funded, anti-Trump dossier.) The emails show one assistant secretary of state saying some of Steele’s reports sound “extreme” and others “do not ring true,” while the U.S. ambassador to Ukraine called some of the Steele reports “flaky.” In May 2020, we forced the declassification and release of the “electronic communication [ used to launch Crossfire Hurricane, written by former FBI official Peter Strzok. In April 2020, we obtained emails [] between former FBI official Peter Strzok and former FBI attorney Lisa Page, including an email dated January 10, 2017, in which Strzok said that the version of the Steele dossier published by BuzzFeed was “identical” to the version given to the FBI by McCain and had “differences” from the dossier provided to the FBI by Fusion GPS co-founder Glenn Simpson and Mother Jones reporter David Corn. January 10, 2017, is the same day BuzzFeed_ published the anti-Trump dossier by former British spy Christopher Steele. The emails also show Strzok and other FBI agents mocking President Trump a few weeks before he was inaugurated. In addition, the emails revealed that Strzok communicated with then-Deputy Director Andrew McCabe about the “leak investigation” tied to the Clinton Foundation (the very leak in which McCabe was later implicated). In September 2019, we released State Department records [] revealing that Steele had an extensive and close working relationship dating back to May of 2014 with high-ranking Obama State Department officials including Jonathan Winer and Victoria Nuland. In August 2019, we obtained “302” report materia [ [] from 2016 FBI interviews of Associate Deputy U.S. Attorney Bruce Ohr, who was removed from his position in December 2017. (A Form 302 is used by FBI agents to memorialize interviews they undertake during an investigation.) In a November 22, 2016, interview, Ohr said that “reporting on Trump’s ties to Russia were going to the Clinton Campaign, Jon Winer at the U.S. State Department and the FBI.” In a late September 2016 interview, Ohr described a person (likely Christopher Steele) as “desperate that Donald Trump not get elected and was passionate about him not being the U.S. President.” A report states that “Ohr knew that [Fusion GPS’s] Glen Simpson and others were talking to Victoria Nuland at the U.S. State Department.” In July 2019, we obtained records [] revealing a September 2016 email exchange between then-Assistant Secretary of State Victoria Nuland and Special Coordinator for Libya Jonathan Winer, a close associate of dossier author Christopher Steele, discussing a “face-to-face” meeting on a “Russian matter.” In August 2018, the Justice Department admitted in a court filing [] that the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court held no hearings on the FISA spy warrant applications targeting Carter Page, a former Trump campaign part-time advisor who was the subject of four controversial FISA warrants. In July 2018, we released records [] about FISA warrants targeting Page, which appeared to confirm that the FBI and DOJ misled the FISA court by withholding material information showing that Hillary Clinton’s campaign and the DNC were behind the “intelligence” used to persuade the court to approve the FISA warrants targeting the Trump team. Taxpayer-Funded NIH Grant Backed Gender-Affirming Care for Youth Despite President Trump’s executive order prohibiting federal funds from promoting gender ideology, a National Institutes of Health grant that began under the Biden administration continued to provide funding for research into gender-affirming care for youth living in rural communities. Our Corruption Chronicles blog exposes [] the details. Charged with making important discoveries that improve health and save lives, the nation’s medical research agency gave a pediatrician and professor at a public university nearly half a million dollars to research gender-affirming care for youth in rural communities who identify as black, indigenous, or people of color (BIPOC). The National Institutes of Health (NIH), which annually disburses tens of billions of dollars [] in research grants, initiated the award during the Biden administration but some of the money flowed under Trump, even after the president banned taxpayer dollars for such initiatives advanced by the left. “Federal funds shall not be used to promote gender ideology,” reads an order [] [ by Trump on the day of his 2025 inauguration. “Each agency shall assess grant conditions and grantee preferences and ensure grant funds do not promote gender ideology.” In this case the NIH, which is part of the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), awarded a Seattle doctor and professor at the University of Washington $428,296 to “advance health equity by increasing health services research involving transgender and gender diverse youth, youth who identify as black, indigenous, or people of color (BIPOC), and youth living in rural communities,” according to the grant announcement []. The government spending data reveals that the agency disbursed $143,000 in fiscal year 2025, even though the president banned public financing for projects like this that clearly promote gender ideology. “Gender diverse youth (GDY) who identify as BIPOC, as well as those living in rural communities, are more likely to experience depression and anxiety than their peers,” the NIH grant states. “Additionally, BIPOC and rural GDY are disproportionately underrepresented in pediatric gender clinics, limiting their access to pediatric gender-affirming care, which has been shown to improve mental health outcomes.” The doctor and professor of pediatrics, Gina Sequeira, who is conducting the study is the co-director of the Seattle Children’s Gender Clinic and specializes in gender-affirming care for children. She was the focus of a lengthy 2022 article [] [ a national news magazine that claimed pediatricians who serve trans youth face increasing harassment. “Lifesaving care could be on the line,” the story proclaimed, adding that only a small group of pediatricians provide gender affirming care in the United States. Sequeira is well-known for conducting research that identifies barriers to gender-affirming care for transgender adolescents and believes pediatricians should “open a door to have a conversation with young people about how they see their gender” [] during routine well-visits. “My hope is one day we get to a place where every clinician, regardless of their specialty, has the basic knowledge and skills to be able to conduct a visit with a transgender patient without hesitation and without the patient being made to feel uncomfortable or disrespected because of their identity,” Sequeira says. Her recent NIH-funded study is supposed to examine how gender specialists who practice in large academic medical centers can connect with underage trans patients throughout the country. Sequeira will build on her existing research with transgender youth and their families to identify existing barriers preventing trans and BIPOC youth in rural communities from receiving gender-affirming care and design as well as implement access to care via telehealth. She is also charged with developing a technology-based enhanced gender support platform to facilitate a comprehensive gender-affirming care provision in the community pediatric setting. “Given few providers have received training in this area and most lack opportunities to consult with transgender specialists, telehealth modalities like telemedicine and electronic consultation show great potential in facilitating the provision of community-based gender-affirming care,” the NIH grant announcement states. It is highly unlikely that American taxpayers will fund this type of research for the remainder of the Trump administration considering that earlier this year the White House officially ended the “Transgender for Everybody [ [ created by Democrats. Under the new policy the president declared it the official practice of the U.S. government that there are only two immutable sexes: male and female. “President Trump banned federal funding, sponsorship, or promotion of the chemical and surgical mutilation of minors—protecting children from irreversible harm and directing agencies to defund institutions engaged in these practices,” according to the White House press release outlining the policy in late March. name: Mary Trump
subject: My uncle is a weak man
disclaimer_text: Paid for by VPP
body:
| [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/118818?t=6&akid=26552%2E878179%2EvtKpd5) Friend, this is Mary Trump.

You may know me as the author of _Too Much and Never Enough_ , or as someone who has spent years sounding the alarm about my uncle, Donald.

[I've launched Transcend PAC to fund the candidates fighting Donald's corruption every day, who will strengthen the democracy my uncle is trying to destroy. If you can give, please split a donation between Transcend PAC and the Voter Protection Project, and then read on to learn why I believe this moment calls for something transformational.](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/118818?t=7&akid=26552%2E878179%2EvtKpd5) | [BECOME A FOUNDING DONOR TODAY »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/118818?t=8&akid=26552%2E878179%2EvtKpd5)
---
* * *
**Here's what I need you to understand about my uncle: Donald is a weak man.**

That might seem like an odd thing to say about somebody who holds such a powerful position, but that's exactly the danger. Every day, as Donald deteriorates – psychologically, emotionally, and cognitively – he grows more desperate, increasing the risk to the rest of us.

Strong people do not rig the system in their favor. They don't silence critics. They don't seek to control the institutions designed to hold them accountable. **Donald does all of those things — because he has to, and he knows it. His behavior isn't evidence of strength – it's evidence of its absence.**

The comprehensiveness with which Donald and the complicit Republican party are attempting to dismantle our institutions and take away our rights, in service to maintaining their hold on power and self-enrichment, should also make clear what is at stake.

Under Donald’s so-called leadership, the Republicans in Congress have stood by while our nation’s alliances have become strained; illegal wars have been started; and our institutions have been weakened and, in some cases, dismantled entirely.

I believe we are going to prevail. But when corrupt leaders like Donald and the sycophantic enablers in his inner circle go unchecked or unchallenged, they can do enormous damage. The antidote is to assemble a coalition of people who refuse to look away and are willing to take action.

**That’s why I’m launching Transcend PAC. Together, we’ll fund candidates who believe in public service and who will work to fulfill the promise of American democracy.** Because we deserve representatives who understand what’s at stake and are prepared to meet the moment.

[If you're able, please split a donation between Transcend PAC and the Voter Protection Project today. Your contributions fund organizing, accountability work, and candidates who understand what’s at stake and are ready to meet the moment. Every dollar will go toward undoing the damage my uncle and the Republican Party have done so we, together, can build something better.](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/118818?t=9&akid=26552%2E878179%2EvtKpd5)

And if tomorrow
or tomorrow
or tomorrow
the target on my back becomes
suddenly real
suddenly deadly
some finger
on some trigger
or some threshold
in some prompt
decides that I'm
a problem
to be solved
in the simplest way

what will live of me

what will live in my children

what will live in my family

what will live with roots in soil

what will live in
the memories of friends

what will live in
the hearts of people

what will live in
the goodness of earth

let it be
if I may hope
if I may choose
if I may strive

let it be
courage
let it be
vision
let it be
reassurance
let it be
solidarity
let it be
dedication
let it be
hope
let it be
life

and love
of life

power dislikes
the inconvenient

those who ask
the real questions

give
the real answers

name
the real names

and will not be silent

will not give in

will not sell out

power dislikes
inconvenience

well isn't that just
too bad

A huge shadow stretched over paradegoers in Buffalo County on the Fourth of July. The source? A massive flag celebrating America's 250th birthday. Buffalo County Republicans passed out over 200 flags, 500 stickers/buttons, and innumerable buckets of candy. They then set up camp four days later to assist alongside Jake Laehn for Sheriff and Sen. Rob Stafsholt at a successful fundraiser for Assemblyman Treig Pronschinske. Auctioneer-turned-Secretary of State candidate Nate Pollnow even proved he hasn't lost a step by auctioning off a few items! **Calumet County**
As the morning dawned on Monday, June 22nd, the Republican Party of Calumet County officially teed off its 3rd Annual Golf Outing at Chilton's Hickory Hills Country Club. Twenty hopeful teams of golfers took the course, supported throughout the day by great food, beautiful weather, events, raffles, and Congressman Tony Wied.
Calumet County GOP also debuted their new elephant float 'Gus' the day prior at the Chilton Father's Day Parade, accompanied by Sheriff Brett Bowe and State Rep. Ron Tusler. **Dodge County**
Dodge County Republicans celebrated an evening of food and patriotic fellowship, gathering to catch up during a classic Wisconsin fish fry. **Door County**
Our endorsed Republican candidate for Governor, Tom Tiffany, made a trip to speak at the Door County Republicans' "Cheers to 250 Years" celebration this past Saturday, July 11th. You can view a clip of his speech **[here.](https://republicanpartyofwisconsin.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fejlyk-didthutlhu-t/)** **Lincoln County**
Republicans of Lincoln County spent their Tuesday canvassing for the Tiffany campaign. **Monroe County**
Monroe County Republicans marched in two parades over the past two weeks: the Tomah Independence Day Parade on July 4th (joined by Sen. Patrick Testin and Rep. Nancy VanderMeer) and the Wilton Weenie Days Parade on July 12th. **Rusk County**
On Sunday, July 12th, paradegoers at the village of Bruce's Blue Hills Festival witnessed Rusk County Republicans supporting state and local candidates! **Sauk County**
Sauk County Republicans put in great work for conservative politics in the county. They worked a table at the Sauk County Fair and represented at the Fourth of July Blackhawk Parade, reaching thousands of people! **Sheboygan County**
Sheboygan County GOP: "As we celebrated Independence Day and the beginning of our nation's 250th year, we were honored to walk alongside so many friends, neighbors, and fellow patriots in the Sheboygan Independence Day Parade. Seeing thousands of smiling faces waving flags, families gathered together, veterans receiving well-deserved applause, and children celebrating the freedoms we often take for granted was both humbling and inspiring." Incredible work! **St. Croix County**
St. Croix County Republicans, as always, had lots to do over the past two weeks. At the Hudson Booster Days on July 4th, members not only participated in the Booster Days Parade with Rep. Shannon Zimmerman, but also worked a pop-up sidewalk tent selling America 250/GOP shirts, hats, stickers, etc. Six days later, St. Croix GOP and Rep. Zimmerman were literally back on the road, walking in the River Falls Days Parade alongside Pierce County Republicans. On July 12th, St. Croix Republican-run **[Faith, Family, Freedom Fest](https://republicanpartyofwisconsin.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fejlyk-didthutlhu-i/)** kicked off, featuring (among others) Rachel Campos-Duffy, Secretary of State Candidate Nate Pollnow, Rep. Zimmerman, other state and national representatives, senators, and countless more. The same day (!), members marched in the New Richmond Fun Fest Parade with Rep. Rob Kreibich and Michael Alfonso. To round it off, the party held a Team Tiffany Tuesday two days after. Incredible work! **Taylor County**
On Thursday, July 9th, Taylor County Republicans gathered to celebrate at their annual Summer Picnic. Notable attendees included Governor candidate Tom Tiffany, Attorney General candidate Eric Toney, and, of course, the great members of the Taylor County Republican Party. **Washburn County**
Washburn County GOP represented at the Spooner Rodeo Parade this past weekend. Check out a recording of the patriotic helicopter flyover coordinated by WCRP Chairman Brian Melton **[here!](https://republicanpartyofwisconsin.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fejlyk-didthutlhu-d/)** **Waukesha County**
Waukesha County GOP did not slow down after their back-to-back parade day on June 28th. Over the weekend of the Fourth, they walked SIX parade routes: Oconomowoc and Eagle on Friday the 3rd; Waukesha, Stone Bank, New Berlin, and Pewaukee on Saturday the 4th. To round off the tour, Waukesha Republicans marched in the Sussex Lions Daze Parade on Sunday, the 12th. Additionally, pictured below is their July 8th Pints n' Politics night.
Phenomenal dedication from Waukesha County! For years, spotting an email scam felt easy. Bad grammar, a fake logo, an obvious ask, and you'd catch it. But the cybercrime frauds that drained nearly $21 billion from Americans last year didn't look sloppy at all. They looked like they came from your bank, your pharmacy, even your own family, and adults over 60 lost the most of anyone. In today's episode of _The Flyover Podcast_ , Amy breaks down five quick inbox moves that clean up your clutter and quietly lock scammers out. ## Fires Continue To Choke States with Smoke, Haze
Smoke from nearly 900 wildfires in Canada and several large blazes in Minnesota is continuing to trigger air quality alerts across more than a dozen states, blanketing the Midwest and Northeast in a thick, dangerous haze. [You can see photos here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2O2zAUBODTUB0N_kmUCxYBAnVOEwQpBcrv0XoJRXpJ2oL29Av7ClsPMJhv_l7mi6dI6fbLb-hayHPCvUZsDctct_wffcTS6r5iwYqJcqmRZiXUwIXlcpzBUzxm04ELiAp1h07a0ejhrKTtVoe9DhLCqAfTL0JICQpAgdZeSex705F7tQkrRynE0NsTCB-CXEZrz2IZPTAjEKjlcvqXKbUVQzzyE8vpmrcuurW1e2X6B1MTU5Nfri_BK2Nq-vObqenqkwfPd4oQqCB_s_hSKN0qf6QVfWzrwT0V_vHwkdrBIX9iYmqqLZeD6YmA6Z9Sm9H0SpquOLjvFCPVwTIjbpun-F7TvnXh06mvAAAA__8Sg4Yu). Philadelphia declared a Code Purple air quality emergency Friday, with the smoke expected to reach from Detroit to Washington, D.C. Chicago and Pittsburgh both declared air quality alerts. Parts of northern Minnesota recorded [Air Quality Index readings above 1,000](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkTGP2zAMhX-NvdGQdI6lDB66ZLuuHQ3GomK2spST6BPy7wunP6ELQYDge_je-_W5fCJHTo-fuNMsIS-JWo0kQmWpe_5DGKlIbRsVqpQ4lxp5McpMoCxot3jk-FrG3s-ByNBHT7O2bvyYrkbbfpudM1ZTuKNZnb1cFK7OXklhuAbU1lx6nk81ZbXTSk0XO3iFIei7s_aq7g59NyryLLkMvzMn2SjEV_6mMqx57-O8iTxr9_GjM7fO3Fprwwu3nM9rZ24nTmduxzmwCK-Rzk0gElYBbaEKClU4kqcCyAW-DowsL_hHDlhhxYSeMUHj6AMXgnc0UJ-F0FfgBLIR7OwbVQFMHlIusr0tCnLl9ICvg6pwThXwng95f7Rcoof1eELghBG0G62y0zQNm-yxL7N_No6R62S7UT125Pimlv-q6ns2fwMAAP__bE-uJQ) on Thursday, the highest in the country. An AQI over 100 is considered unhealthy, and a reading over 300 is hazardous. Officials are monitoring conditions ahead of Sunday's World Cup Final at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, which has been affected by smoke conditions. You can [see maps of the smoke's impact here.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2S6yAMhZ_G7vAA_sEpKG6TLrfd0oODHGsXgwdpw-btd8grbKeZT9KZ73zclpvDgPHx3x1geUtLhEIBmCEvdKQvcAEyU9khA0HElCngoqWehDRCzYt3GF7L0Hq7AWjoW7DKzEM_XbQy7W7nfl1N78fVjArUCG5URg8Xrdx0H0anW7T1mzRqVlJOo-m8dNum1tmYi1xn55tBgkdOuftMGHmHLbzSE3J3T0cb7M58UtP_a_S10ddSSndfqVpU3uhrHSvA4DfMQOKtJQ4MAVMkAT9nIvDiQF-AWMSUeQdHLL7rXZutP0tdpsk0g3wcDsM7mv_U19Pq3wAAAP__TP2B-A)
## New US Strikes Hit Strategic Sites in Iran
The U.S. hit [bridges, energy sites, and a port surveillance tower](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OpDAQhJ8GMiPb_BgCB5eQzaUXojZuhr4x9qjtGTT79Cv2FTatTypVff9uyw0oULz_hQNt2dIS8cwBS0Fe8pEeCAG55HNHxoyREudAi5Z6ENIINS4eKHyWrvZ2Q9TY1miVGbt2mLQy9W7bYV1N1zvnnHGgpg62rTW9QiWnvu9kTfZqk0aNSsqhN42XsG3KjcZM0o3gq06ip5K4-Z8olh238Elv5GZNRx3sXsozV-2fSs-Vns_zbKJbrxcXv5LEwVd6JoZY6fmVRS5MD8zCMfk7ZnER8UxcxJ74eH0JB9EDC3AOssgfJhC8RuhHM_VTzdY_TwqB8mCqTt4PoPCzpfxK4Nvq7wAAAP___U-HRg) across southern Iran overnight, marking a seventh consecutive night of strikes aimed at pressuring Tehran to relinquish control of the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. Central Command said it struck dozens of targets including air defense sites and military logistics infrastructure.
